steps.label: Breast composition
steps.detail: Record breast composition (A–D) and whether density could mask a lesion.
steps.look: CC and MLO views of both breasts together; tomosynthesis when acquired.
steps.normal: The breasts are [almost entirely fatty / scattered fibroglandular density] (category [A / B]).
findings: Heterogeneously dense breasts, which may obscure small masses (category C).
Extremely dense breasts, which lower the sensitivity of mammography (category D).
steps.tip: Dense tissue can mask a lesion; a negative mammogram does not resolve a palpable abnormality.

steps.label: Masses
steps.detail: Describe any mass by side, clock position or quadrant, depth, size, shape, margin and density.
steps.look: Both projections: a mass is seen on two views with convex outward borders; spot compression or tomosynthesis for margins.
steps.normal: No suspicious mass.
findings: [Right] breast [upper outer quadrant, 10 o'clock], [middle] depth: [oval / round / irregular] mass __ mm with [circumscribed / obscured / microlobulated / indistinct / spiculated] margins, [high / equal / low / fat-containing] density.
Fat-containing mass (e.g., lipoma, oil cyst, hamartoma).
steps.tip: Spiculated or indistinct margins and irregular shape are the most suspicious mass features.

steps.label: Asymmetry and architectural distortion
steps.detail: Classify any asymmetry (asymmetry, global, focal, developing) and look for architectural distortion.
steps.look: Compare both breasts side by side and with prior studies; confirm persistence on additional views or tomosynthesis.
steps.normal: No architectural distortion or suspicious asymmetry.
findings: Focal asymmetry in the [ ] seen on both views, [persistent / resolving] on spot compression.
Developing asymmetry: new or larger since [date].
Architectural distortion at [ ] without a history of surgery at that site.
Summation (superimposed tissue) resolving on additional views.
steps.tip: A developing asymmetry has a meaningful malignancy rate and usually needs further work-up.

steps.label: Calcifications and associated features
steps.detail: Describe calcification morphology and distribution, and skin, nipple, trabecular and axillary findings.
steps.look: Magnification views for morphology; distribution across the whole breast; skin, nipple and axillary tail.
steps.normal: No suspicious calcifications; skin, nipple and axillae unremarkable.
findings: Typically benign calcifications ([vascular / coarse / rod-like / rim / skin / layering]).
[Amorphous / coarse heterogeneous / fine pleomorphic / fine linear or fine-linear branching] calcifications in a [grouped / linear / segmental / regional] distribution spanning __ mm.
Skin thickening and trabecular thickening of the [ ] breast.
Enlarged dense axillary node without fatty hilum.
steps.tip: Linear or segmental distribution follows a duct and raises suspicion even for less suspicious morphology.

steps.label: Correlation and assessment
steps.detail: Correlate with the clinical site and prior studies and give the final BI-RADS category with the matching management.
steps.look: Clinical marker or site; prior studies of comparable projection.
steps.normal: No mammographic abnormality at the clinical site; stable compared with [date]. BI-RADS 1: negative.
findings: BI-RADS 0: incomplete — additional imaging [views / ultrasound] needed.
BI-RADS 2: benign finding(s).
BI-RADS 3: probably benign — short-interval follow-up.
BI-RADS 4 / 5: suspicious / highly suggestive of malignancy — tissue sampling recommended.
steps.tip: The final category and the recommendation must match.

steps.label: Localisation
steps.detail: Map each lesion by side, clock position, distance from the nipple and depth.
steps.look: Radial and antiradial scans; record the clock face and distance from the nipple in cm.
steps.normal: No focal lesion in the area examined.
findings: [Right] breast [10 o'clock], __ cm from the nipple, [superficial / middle / posterior] depth.
steps.tip: Correlate the ultrasound location with the mammographic and clinical site; a mismatch means the finding may be different.

steps.label: Shape, orientation and margin
steps.detail: Describe shape, orientation and margins.
steps.look: Two orthogonal planes: parallel (wider than tall) or not parallel; circumscribed or not.
findings: Oval, parallel, circumscribed mass __ × __ × __ mm.
Irregular, not parallel (taller than wide) mass with [angular / microlobulated / indistinct / spiculated] margins.
steps.tip: Not-parallel orientation and non-circumscribed margins are the most suspicious ultrasound features.

steps.label: Echo pattern and posterior features
steps.detail: Assess the echo pattern, posterior features and calcifications.
steps.look: Compare the echogenicity with fat; look behind the lesion for enhancement or shadowing.
findings: Anechoic simple cyst with posterior enhancement.
Complicated cyst with homogeneous low-level echoes.
Hypoechoic solid mass with posterior shadowing and an echogenic rim.
Complex cystic and solid mass.

steps.label: Vascularity and associated features
steps.detail: Review Doppler, ducts, skin and surrounding tissue.
steps.look: Colour Doppler with low pressure; adjacent ducts, skin thickness and oedema.
steps.normal: No internal vascularity; ducts, skin and surrounding tissue normal.
findings: Internal vascularity on Doppler.
Duct extension from the mass.
Skin thickening and oedema of the [ ].

steps.label: Nodes and assessment
steps.detail: Assess the axillary nodes and give the BI-RADS assessment with recommendation.
steps.look: Axilla: cortical thickness, hilum and shape of each node.
steps.normal: Axillary nodes normal with a thin cortex and fatty hilum. BI-RADS [1 / 2].
findings: Axillary node with cortical thickening of __ mm [and effaced hilum].
BI-RADS 3: probably benign; follow-up in [ ] months.
BI-RADS 4: suspicious; ultrasound-guided biopsy recommended.
steps.tip: A negative targeted ultrasound does not cancel a suspicious finding on another modality.

steps.label: Index tumour
steps.detail: Localise the known malignancy and measure its extent.
steps.look: The modality that shows the tumour best (mammography, ultrasound or MRI); biopsy clip position.
findings: Known [right] breast carcinoma at [ ], __ mm, with biopsy clip in the lesion.

steps.label: Additional disease and span
steps.detail: Assess separate foci, associated calcifications and the total disease span; check the contralateral breast.
steps.look: Measure from the furthest edge of related disease; contralateral breast on the same examination.
steps.normal: No additional ipsilateral or contralateral disease.
findings: Associated calcifications extend __ mm beyond the mass (total span __ mm).
Additional focus in the same quadrant (multifocal) / different quadrant (multicentric).
Contralateral finding: [ ].
steps.tip: Report the index lesion and the total span separately; surgery is planned on both.

steps.label: Skin, nipple and chest wall
steps.detail: Describe skin, nipple, pectoralis and chest wall relationships.
steps.look: Posterior margin against the pectoralis; skin and nipple.
steps.normal: No skin, nipple, pectoralis or chest wall involvement.
findings: Skin thickening and oedema (inflammatory pattern) over the [ ].
Nipple retraction and involvement.
Invasion of the pectoralis muscle without chest wall invasion.
steps.tip: Pectoralis involvement alone is not chest wall invasion; chest wall means ribs, intercostal muscles or serratus anterior.

steps.label: Regional nodes
steps.detail: Map suspicious axillary nodes by level and internal mammary and supraclavicular nodes.
steps.look: Axillary levels I–III relative to pectoralis minor; internal mammary chain; supraclavicular fossa.
steps.normal: No suspicious axillary, internal mammary or supraclavicular nodes.
findings: Suspicious level [I] axillary node with cortical thickening __ mm [clip placed].
Enlarged internal mammary node __ mm.
Supraclavicular node __ mm.

steps.label: Distant disease and response
steps.detail: Report the distant sites covered and, when restaging, the response compared with baseline.
steps.look: Staging CT, bone imaging or PET-CT when available; baseline for comparison.
steps.normal: No distant disease within the imaged field.
findings: Liver / bone / lung lesions suspicious for metastases.
Partial response: index tumour decreased from __ to __ mm.

steps.label: Implant type and position
steps.detail: Identify silicone or saline implants and their position relative to the pectoralis muscle.
steps.look: MRI silicone-selective sequences or ultrasound; mammography with implant-displacement (Eklund) views.
steps.normal: Bilateral [silicone / saline] implants in [subglandular / subpectoral] position.
findings: [Single / double] lumen [silicone / saline] implant on the [right].

steps.label: Shell and contour
steps.detail: Inspect implant contour and shell integrity; separate radial folds from rupture.
steps.look: MRI and ultrasound along the implant surface.
steps.normal: Smooth implant contour; normal radial folds only.
findings: Focal contour bulge (herniation) of the [ ] implant.
Radial fold extending to the outer shell (normal).
steps.tip: Radial folds extend to the periphery of the implant; a rupture line floats inside the gel.

steps.label: Intracapsular rupture
steps.detail: Assess the implant contents for signs of intracapsular rupture.
steps.look: MRI silicone-selective images; ultrasound for stepladder echoes.
steps.normal: No signs of intracapsular rupture.
findings: Intracapsular rupture: curvilinear lines within the gel (linguine sign).
Stepladder sign on ultrasound.
Droplets of water within silicone (salad-oil sign) — possible early rupture.
steps.tip: The linguine sign — collapsed shell floating in the gel — is the most reliable sign of intracapsular rupture.

steps.label: Extracapsular silicone and peri-implant fluid
steps.detail: Look for silicone beyond the capsule, peri-implant fluid and capsular masses.
steps.look: MRI and ultrasound around the capsule and into the breast; late peri-implant fluid raises BIA-ALCL concern.
steps.normal: No extracapsular silicone, peri-implant fluid or capsular mass.
findings: Extracapsular silicone in the [ ] breast (snowstorm on ultrasound).
Late peri-implant effusion __ mm; aspiration for cytology (CD30) is advised to exclude BIA-ALCL.
Capsular mass __ mm.
steps.tip: A late seroma (more than one year after surgery) needs aspiration for BIA-ALCL.

steps.label: Breast and nodes
steps.detail: Assess the surrounding breast tissue and regional nodes within the study scope.
steps.look: Breast parenchyma and axillae; silicone in nodes.
steps.normal: No suspicious breast finding; axillary nodes normal.
findings: Silicone-laden axillary node.
Breast finding: [ ].
Implant-integrity MRI without contrast: breast cancer assessment not included.

steps.label: Symptomatic site
steps.detail: Identify the palpable or symptomatic site and relate it to the nipple.
steps.look: Mammography with a skin marker; targeted ultrasound.
steps.normal: No abnormality at the symptomatic site.
findings: Palpable abnormality in the [right] [retroareolar / eccentric] region.

steps.label: Retroareolar tissue
steps.detail: Distinguish gynaecomastia (nodular, dendritic or diffuse) from fatty enlargement.
steps.look: Retroareolar density centred behind the nipple; compare both sides.
steps.normal: Normal male breast with fat only; no gynaecomastia.
findings: Nodular gynaecomastia: fan-shaped retroareolar density [unilateral / bilateral].
Dendritic gynaecomastia with branching strands.
Pseudogynaecomastia: fatty enlargement without glandular tissue.
steps.tip: Gynaecomastia is centred behind the nipple; an eccentric mass is not gynaecomastia until proven otherwise.

steps.label: Focal lesion
steps.detail: Describe any eccentric or discrete mass separately.
steps.look: Mammography and ultrasound of any mass eccentric to the nipple.
steps.normal: No discrete mass.
findings: Eccentric irregular mass __ mm with [spiculated / indistinct] margins, suspicious for carcinoma.
Circumscribed mass __ mm (e.g., epidermal inclusion cyst, lipoma).

steps.label: Nipple and skin
steps.detail: Look for nipple retraction, skin lesions and inflammatory change.
steps.look: Nipple and skin on mammography and ultrasound.
steps.normal: Nipple and skin normal.
findings: Nipple retraction.
Skin thickening over the mass.
Subareolar abscess.

steps.label: Nodes and correlation
steps.detail: Review axillary nodes and concordance between imaging and clinical findings; give the assessment.
steps.look: Axilla on ultrasound.
steps.normal: Axillary nodes normal. BI-RADS [1 / 2].
findings: Suspicious axillary node.
BI-RADS 4/5: biopsy recommended.

steps.label: Background and quality
steps.detail: Assess the amount of fibroglandular tissue, background parenchymal enhancement and technical quality.
steps.look: Precontrast T1 for fibroglandular tissue; early subtraction for background enhancement; check motion and registration.
steps.normal: [Scattered] fibroglandular tissue with [minimal] background parenchymal enhancement; no significant artefact.
findings: [Marked] background parenchymal enhancement, reducing sensitivity.
Motion or misregistration limits the subtraction images.

steps.label: Lesion location
steps.detail: Identify each finding by side, quadrant or clock position, depth and size.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal subtraction images.
steps.normal: No suspicious enhancing finding.
findings: Finding 1: [right] breast [ ] o'clock, __ cm from the nipple, [ ] depth, __ mm.

steps.label: Mass or non-mass enhancement
steps.detail: Distinguish focus, mass and non-mass enhancement and describe shape, margin, distribution and internal pattern.
steps.look: Early subtraction and MIP images.
findings: Irregular mass with spiculated margins and heterogeneous / rim enhancement.
Oval circumscribed mass with dark internal septations (fibroadenoma pattern).
Non-mass enhancement in a [segmental / linear] distribution with clumped internal enhancement.
steps.tip: Segmental or linear clumped non-mass enhancement is suspicious for DCIS.

steps.label: Signal and kinetics
steps.detail: Correlate T2 signal, diffusion and the enhancement time course.
steps.look: T2, DWI/ADC and time–intensity curves.
findings: High T2 signal, no restricted diffusion, persistent enhancement (favours benign).
Low T2 signal, restricted diffusion (ADC __) and washout kinetics (suspicious).
steps.tip: Kinetics and diffusion support, but do not replace, morphological assessment.

steps.label: Extent and assessment
steps.detail: Review total span, skin, nipple, chest wall and nodes, then give the MRI BI-RADS assessment.
steps.look: Sagittal images for span and chest wall; axillae.
steps.normal: No skin, nipple or chest wall involvement; normal nodes. BI-RADS [1 / 2].
findings: Total extent of disease __ mm.
Invasion of the pectoralis / chest wall.
BI-RADS [4 / 5 / 6] with recommendation [ ].
